<thought>The Friedel‑Crafts acylation replaces an aryl halide (aryl‑Cl) with an acyl group derived from an acyl chloride, forming a ketone on the aromatic ring and breaking the C–Cl bond. In the forward reaction, the functional groups involved are an “aryl halide” that is broken and an “acyl chloride” that is consumed (formed as a reactant). The key new bond is a C–C bond between two sp² carbons (aromatic‑aryl to carbonyl carbon), which is a 6‑6 bond. Using these valid functional‑group terms should retrieve the appropriate retrosynthetic template.</thought>
<action>search_template_catalog_by_criteria</action>
<action_input>{
    "molecule_smiles": "COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CCl)cc3)c2N)c1",
    "functional_groups_broken": ["aryl halide"],
    "functional_groups_formed": ["acyl chloride"],
    "bonds_formed": ["6-6"],
    "limit": 5
}</action_input>
